evidence.summary: Header comment and ACCOUNTS dict: accounts are keyed by (provider, subject); each holds id, email and role 'member'; the provider sends email and email_verified.

callback() creates an account the first time a (provider, subject) pair is seen, with id 'lu-<n>', the email as given and role 'member', and returns the account; email_verified is accepted but never used.

architecture.backend: single Python module with an in-memory dict; the OAuth redirect and token exchange are not in the source

features.name: Sign in with an OAuth provider
features.description: Sign in through a Google-style provider; the first sign-in creates an account.
features.observed_behaviour: callback(provider, subject, email, email_verified) looks up the account by (provider, subject); if missing it creates one with id 'lu-<n>', the email and role 'member'. It returns the account record; no session or token is issued.
features.business_logic: Identity is the (provider, subject) pair, not the email. The email is stored as given (not normalised). email_verified is ignored. No linking to any other account. Default role 'member'.
features.integration: Needs the unified user store, account linking rules, a session, and a real provider adapter (redirect, code exchange, ID-token checks are not in the source).

entities.name: Account
entities.description: A person who signs in through an OAuth provider, identified by provider and subject

fields.name: subject
fields.description: the provider's user id; part of the lookup key

fields.name: email
fields.description: as sent by the provider, not normalised, not unique

auth.session: none in the source (callback returns the account record)

integrations.name: OAuth provider
integrations.purpose: federated sign-in; supplies subject, email and email_verified

error_handling.behaviour: returns the existing account for the same (provider, subject)

unknowns: The OAuth redirect, code exchange and ID-token signature checks are not in the source; the callback trusts its arguments. A real provider cannot be exercised here (no network, no provider account).
What the 'member' role may do: Linkup has no permission checks.
Licence: the user says MIT, but sources/linkup contains no licence file, so code reuse is recorded as not-allowed until a licence file is supplied (the feature is rebuilt anyway).
